title: Days of the Week & Months
description: Learn the seven days of the week, the twelve months of the year, and capitalization rules.
objectives: Name and spell all seven days of the week in chronological order
Name and spell all twelve months of the year accurately
Apply the strict English rule: Days and Months MUST always be capitalized (Monday, July)

vocabularyList.definition: The day of the week before Tuesday and following Sunday; the start of the working week.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Our new course starts on Monday morning.

vocabularyList.definition: The day of the week before Saturday and following Thursday.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Jummah prayers take place on Friday afternoon.

vocabularyList.definition: The day of the week before Monday and following Saturday; a weekend day.
The first month of the year, in the northern hemisphere usually the coldest.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Winter is very cold in January in Quetta.

vocabularyList.definition: The third month of the year; marks the beginning of spring.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Pakistan Day is celebrated on the 23rd of March.

vocabularyList.definition: The eighth month of the year, in the northern hemisphere usually warm.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Independence Day is celebrated on 14th August.

vocabularyList.definition: The tenth month of the year, in the northern hemisphere autumn.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The autumn breeze begins in October.

vocabularyList.definition: The twelfth and final month of the year.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Schools close for winter vacation in late December.

vocabularyList.definition: A period of seven consecutive days, typically from Monday to Sunday.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: There are seven days in a week.

vocabularyList.definition: Each of the twelve named periods into which a year is divided.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: There are twelve months in one calendar year.

sections.title: The Calendar Framework & Capitalization
sections.content:
In English, names of days and months are **proper nouns**. This means they have one inviolable rule:

### The Golden Capitalization Rule
Days and months **MUST ALWAYS BEGIN WITH A CAPITAL LETTER**, no matter where they appear in a sentence!
- *I will see you on **M**onday.* (NEVER *monday*).
- *My birthday is in **J**uly.* (NEVER *july*).

callouts.text: The first 'd' in **Wednesday** is completely silent! It is pronounced as two syllables: **/ËˆwenzdeÉª/** (WENZ-day).

callouts.title: Preposition Pairings
callouts.text: Always say **ON** with days (*on Friday*) and **IN** with months (*in August*).

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: Seven days: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday.
CAPITALIZE all days and months always (Monday, August).
Use 'on' with days (on Friday) and 'in' with months (in March).
